event_text: Oklahoma City bombing: Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols are indicted for the bombing. Michael Fortier pleads guilty in a plea-bargain for his testimony.
headline: Oklahoma City Bombing: McVeigh and Nichols Indicted
story: Barry adjusted his feathers, gazing out at the rubble-strewn streets of Oklahoma City. 'Quite the mess, Susan. April 19th, 1995, Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols decided to express their discontent with the government by detonating a truck bomb in front of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building.' Susan blinked slowly. 'Killed 168 people, including children in a daycare centre. Injured over 680. Rather a lot of paperwork to fill out after that, I should think.' Barry nodded. 'And now they're being indicted. McVeigh, the main chap behind it, was rather keen on the idea of a "revolution" against the US government. Nichols, his co-conspirator, seemed to be more of a "I'm just here for the ride" sort of fellow.' Susan ruffled her feathers. 'And then there's Michael Fortier, who pleaded guilty in exchange for testifying against the other two. He was the one who knew about the plot and chose not to warn anyone, but did tell the authorities about it after the fact. How very... convenient.'
regret_line: A spot of hindsight regret might be in order, considering the rather drastic measures taken to make a point.
winner_line: The surveillance state, which gained a considerable foothold in the aftermath of the bombing, paving the way for the USA PATRIOT Act.
